root_cause.text: The BPF constant blinding function `bpf_jit_blind_insn()` does not handle `BPF_ST | BPF_PROBE_MEM32` instruction modes, so immediate stores rewritten from `BPF_MEM` to `BPF_PROBE_MEM32` by `convert_ctx_accesses()` during verification escape blinding when `bpf_jit_harden >= 1`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The blinding switch only matches BPF_ST|BPF_MEM (mode 0x60), not BPF_ST|BPF_PROBE_MEM32 (mode 0xa0). The instruction falls through unblinded." The patch adds four new cases for `BPF_ST | BPF_PROBE_MEM32 | BPF_{B,H,W,DW}` to `bpf_jit_blind_insn()`.

This store of the blinded value is part of the normal blinding sequence; because BPF_ST | BPF_PROBE_MEM32 is not handled, this line is not executed for those instructions, leaving the original immediate unblinded.

The break statement terminates the case for handled modes; the missing case for BPF_ST | BPF_PROBE_MEM32 means the switch block may fall through to a default that does not apply blinding, directly contributing to the vulnerability.
The closing brace marks the end of the switch case block; the absence of a corresponding case for BPF_ST | BPF_PROBE_MEM32 is the structural gap that causes the vulnerability.
